newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Quake hits near Solomon Islands, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Quake hits near Solomon Islands, no casualties.

text.p: An earthquake measuring seven on the open-ended Richter scale struck in the Pacific Ocean south of Papua New Guinea's Bougainville island on Tuesday but no casualties were reported, seismologists said.
The quake, with an epicentre about 50 km (30 miles) south of Bougainville, struck at about 9.26 a.m. (2326 GMT Monday).
Bougainville, the scene of a long-running secessionist rebellion, is located in the Solomon Islands, a chain in the western Pacific northeast of Australia.
"It's offshore on the edge of the Solomon sea plate between the Pacific and the Solomon sea plates," Kevin McCue of the Australian Seismological Centre told Reuters.
"I would think almost undoubtedly there would have been at least a small wave offshore that may do some damage," he said.
McCue said the United States Earthquake Information Service had informed Canberra that the quake was located 7.02 degrees south and 155.47 degrees east at a depth of 33 km (20 miles).
Seismologist Horst Letz of the Port Moresby Geophysical Observatory in Papua New Guinea said it would be very difficult to gauge any damage.
Earthquakes are a relatively common occurrence under the ocean floor around the Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea.
